biography: Ivan Capelli, born under the Mediterranean sun in Bari, Italy, didn't inherit a racing pedigree; his father owned a small vineyard. Yet, the roar of engines always resonated within him. At the age of ten, he disassembled and rebuilt his father's old Vespa far too many times, driven by an innate curiosity about mechanics. His racing career began almost by accident. While assisting a friend at a local karting event, a no-show driver led to Ivan being thrust into the seat. Against all odds, he not only finished but secured a podium, launching his trajectory. Despite showing initial promise with Newcyan Racing, a lack of competitive machinery stifled his progress. A move to Scuderia Forza promised glory, but internal politics and a car ill-suited to his style led to frustration. Now, back with Newcyan, he is striving to elevate the team and prove his worth as a seasoned driver.
drivingStyle: Capelli is a study in controlled aggression. He doesn't possess the raw, flamboyant pace of some, but his meticulous approach to every corner is what sets him apart. He meticulously analyzes data and track conditions, favoring a smooth, consistent style that conserves tires. He builds his pace throughout the race, often setting fastest laps in the closing stages as others fade. This calculated approach allows him to extract maximum performance from the car, even when it lacks outright speed. While not prone to spectacular overtakes, he is a master of positioning and capitalizing on rivals' mistakes.

rivalries.reason: A clash of personalities and driving styles. Alvarez, known for his aggressive moves, has often made contact with Capelli, leading to heated exchanges both on and off the track.
A battle for supremacy within Scuderia Forza. Rodriguez was the team's golden boy, and Capelli's arrival challenged his status, leading to a tense and ultimately unproductive partnership.

Both rose through the ranks of Italian motorsport together, creating a friendly but fierce rivalry. Bellini often has the faster car, but Capelli's consistency keeps him close in the championship standings.

quirks: Always wears the same faded blue driving gloves, claiming they bring him luck.
Before each race, he listens to a specific aria from a Puccini opera to calm his nerves.
Refuses to eat any kind of seafood on race weekends.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about raw speed; it's about precision, patience, and the ability to anticipate what's coming next. It's a chess match at 300 kilometers per hour."
careerHighlight: Winning the wet-weather Grand Prix at Monza in 2027. Starting from 8th, he masterfully navigated the treacherous conditions, showcasing his exceptional car control and tire management skills, securing his only F1 victory to date.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 2028 Monaco Grand Prix. A momentary lapse in concentration led to contact with the barrier, costing him a potential victory and severely damaging his championship aspirations.
